title: Stable Mechanisms
abstract: arXiv:2603.12532v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study mechanism design environments in which the designer does not know the distribution of agents' private information and draws inferences from the behavior induced by the mechanism itself. A mechanism is stable if it is optimal under some belief consistent with the information it generates, and robustly stable if this property survives small informational perturbations. We establish a fictitious revelation principle: any incentive-compatible mechanism admits a representation as a direct mechanism paired with an information filter, preserving both outcomes and informational content. Applying the framework to the classic monopoly problem, we show that, under regularity of the true type distribution, robustly stable mechanisms coincide with optimal mechanisms under that distribution, as if it were known to the designer. translated_abstract: 我们研究这样的机制设计环境：设计者不知道参与者私人信息的分布，而是从机制本身所诱导的行为中进行推断。如果一个机制在某些与其所产生的信息相一致的信念下是最优的，那么该机制就是稳定的；如果这一性质在小的信息扰动下仍然成立，则称其为稳健稳定的。我们建立了一个虚拟显示原理：任何激励相容机制都可以表示为一个直接机制与信息过滤器的组合，同时保留原有的结果和信息内容。将该框架应用于经典的垄断问题，我们证明在真实类型分布满足正则性条件时，稳健稳定机制与该分布下的最优机制恰好一致，就好像设计者知道该分布一样。然而在一般情况下，标价机制可以在局部收入最大值处保持稳健稳定，因此全局次优的（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了“稳定机制”与“稳健稳定机制”的概念，并建立了虚拟显示原理，证明在正则性条件下稳健稳定的垄断机制表现得如同设计者知道真实类型分布，同时解释了为何次优的标价机制能够在局部收入最大值处持续存在。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the concepts of stable and robustly stable mechanisms along with a fictitious revelation principle, showing that under regularity conditions robustly stable monopoly mechanisms coincide with optimal mechanisms as if the designer knew the true type distribution, while explaining why globally suboptimal posted-price mechanisms can persist at local revenue maxima.
